title.value: Evaluating Montréal’s harm reduction interventions for people who inject drugs: protocol for observational study and cost-effectiveness analysis
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper on evaluating harm reduction interventions in Montréal for people who inject drugs, with an emphasis on both observational study and cost-effectiveness analysis.
title.quote:
Evaluating Montréal’s harm
reduction interventions for
people who inject drugs:
protocol for observational
study and cost-­effectiveness
analysis.

analysis.description: This paper outlines a protocol for conducting a comprehensive cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) of harm reduction interventions for people who inject drugs (PWID) in Montréal, Canada. The study intends to use a variety of data sources to evaluate local effects of interventions such as supervised injection facilities, needle and syringe programs, and opioid agonist treatments. By analyzing these interventions' impact on drug-use-related injuries, infections, and deaths, the research aims to provide evidence on the cost-effectiveness of each intervention from the public healthcare payer’s perspective.

type.justification: The paper describes an empirical study as it involves collecting and analyzing data from real-world interventions and outcomes related to harm reduction for PWID.
